resolutions.researcher_notes: Value 'operating' well supported. sfegypt.com (State Information / petroleum ministry release) states 'وتم تشغيل الخط في مايو 2019 قبل الموعد المحدد بـ 7 أشهر' (line put into operation May 2019, 7 months ahead of schedule). Daily News Egypt (independent English, 20 Nov 2019) confirms 'completion of a pipeline project linking Nooros gas field to Abu Madi and El Gamil ... in May'. Al-Borsa (alborsaanews.com, independent Arabic) independently reports completion 'فى شهر مايو الماضى'. Two+ independent origins agreeing -> high. Dead original petro-news.com/95212 replaced; petro-news wayback also lists the completed line.

No independent (non-GEM) source found that states a 2017 proposal/start year. Ahram (gate.ahram.org.eg/News/1999592, dated 8-8-2018) shows the project under active construction with an executive-status follow-up as of Aug 2018, and sfegypt says it was completed May 2019 '7 months ahead of schedule' (implying a scheduled Dec-2019 finish) — both consistent with a ~2017 start but neither pins the year. WebSearch summaries that say 'construction began in 2017' trace back to the GEM wiki and cannot be cited. Marked UNRESOLVED; ProposalYear=2017 is plausible but not corroborated by any citable independent source.

sfegypt.com explicitly states 'تنفيذ مشروع مد خط بري بطول 130 كم وقطر 24 و 32 بوصة لربط آبار نورس بمحطة الجميل' — 130 km onshore line, diameters 24 and 32 inch. This is the only source giving an exact length; Ahram/Al-Borsa/Daily News describe the two-leg route (Nooros->Abu Madi and Abu Madi->El Gamil) but give no km figure. Single strong primary source -> medium. (Diameter 24/32 inch also available here if needed.)

NOTE: the FuelSource cell value is populated with URL strings, not a fuel-source name (a data-entry quirk in the row). The actual fuel source is the Nooros (نورس) offshore gas field. sfegypt ('لربط آبار نورس'), Al-Borsa (line carries Nooros/نورس production), and Daily News Egypt ('linking Nooros gas field to Abu Madi and El Gamil') all independently confirm the line is fed by the Nooros field, entering the national gas grid. Of the three URLs already sitting in the value: alborsaanews link verifies OK; the enppi.com link 404s; petrojet.com.eg/project-details/30 is a JS single-page app returning no readable content. Provided three working refs supporting the Nooros-field source -> high.

Endpoints strongly corroborated: start = Nooros (نورس) field; end = El Gamil (الجميل) treatment station in Port Said (بورسعيد). sfegypt 'لربط آبار نورس بمحطة الجميل في بورسعيد'; Daily News Egypt 'from the Nooros field ... to the Abu Madi gas treatment plant, and the second from Abu Madi to El Gamil in Port Said'; Al-Borsa 'من المحطة البرية بأبو ماضى إلى المحطة البرية بالجميل ببورسعيد'. Two+ independent -> high for StartLocation=Nooros/Noors, EndPrefecture=El Gamil, EndState=Port Said. CAVEAT: the sheet's StartPrefecture 'Belkas' / StartState 'Dakahlia' are NOT confirmed by these sources — Nooros is an offshore Nile Delta field and the onshore leg runs through Abu Madi (Dakahlia); 'Belkas' district is unverified and may need review.

$300,000,000 USD strongly corroborated across four independent origins: sfegypt 'باستثمارات بلغت حوالى 300 مليون دولار'; Al-Borsa 'بتكلفة 300 مليون دولار'; Daily News Egypt 'at a cost of $300m'; Ahram 'بتكلفة 300 مليون دولار'. -> high. NB: the Ahram piece also cites a separate '380 مليون دولار' figure for the neighbouring Baltim offshore development line — do not conflate; the 300M is stated specifically for Nooros–Abu Madi–El Gamil.

CONTRADICTION FLAG: the sheet lists Owner1 = 'Egyptian Natural Gas Holding Co' (EGAS) at 100%, but no verified source supports EGAS owning this pipeline. Every independent source attributes the field/line to Petrobel (بترول بلاعيم / Belayim Petroleum) as operator-executor — Ahram convened 'رؤساء شركات بتروبل، وإنبي، وبتروجت' and describes the fields as 'التابعة لشركة بترول بلاعيم بتروبل'; Petrobel is the Eni-IEOC (آيوك ~75%) / BP (25%) JV. The gas is pumped into the national grid ('الشبكة القومية للغازات الطبيعية') operated by GASCO, an EGAS subsidiary. EGAS 100% ownership is plausible only as the state gas-holding company but is not stated by any citable source. Marked UNRESOLVED; recommend a human decision on owner attribution (EGAS vs Petrobel/EGPC), do not overwrite blindly.
